the diffusion and reactivities between La0.6Sr0.4MnO3 (LSM) and YSZ, and between LSM and ZrO _{2} are the main reasons for the poor performances and the fast degradation of the SOFC cells.
the electrical performances of the SOFC were limited by the presence of the pyrochlore secondary phase and that it was formed by the diffusion of Mn from the cathode to the electrolyte.
the diffusion of manganese and the formation of pyrochlore are responsible for the drop off of ionic conductivity in the electrolyte.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new SOFC technology based on the co-sintered anode supported cell concept.
a better understanding of diffusion and reaction at the interface between LSM and YZS in planar cells.
the study of the reactivity and the diffusion at the interface between LSM and YSO2 in planar SOFCs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for a given cell, it is not only the microstructure but also the composition of the layers that are important.
the diffusion of manganese and the growth of pyrochlore are responsible for the poor performances of the cells.
the main reason for the observed cell performance is related to the high sintering temperature of the electrolyte (1350 °) and to the diffusion of the manganese through the electrolytes and cathode.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a co-sintering process is not suitable for the fabrication of planar SOFCS, but that it could be used for the fabrication of SOFCs in the form of tubular cells.
the electrolyte thickness is not the only factor that determines cell performance.

the diffusion of manganese and the growth of the resistivity pyrochlore La2ZrZrO7 are the main reasons for the drop off of cell performances, which can only be improved by lowering the co-sintered temperature.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the co-sinters of LSM and YSZ at high temperature should be avoided, and that a two-step sintering process should be used.
it is possible to use TEM to characterize the interfaces of SOFCs with an electrolyte layer thickness down to 40 μM.

the co-soldering temperature of LSM and YSZ must be reduced to avoid the detrimental diffusion of Mn through the electrolyte, and that the cell should be operated in order to avoid any further diffusion of Mn through LSM.
